bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar SIR Judgment Clarifies That Electoral Roll Exclusion Won't Result In Loss Of Other Rights
bihar_raw_news.content: Login Account Subscribe Premium Home / Top Stories / Bihar SIR Judgment Clarifies That... Bihar SIR Judgment Clarifies That Electoral Roll Exclusion Won't Result In Loss Of Other Rights : Supreme Court Debby Jain 25 Aug 2026 4:19 PM IST Share this Listen to this Article The Supreme Court on Tuesday orally said that its judgment in the Bihar SIR matter has held that the deletion from the electoral roll per se will not lead to the loss of other citizenship benefits. During the hearing of the West Bengal SIR matter today, the Court was told that persons excluded from electoral rolls are being deprived of ration under the Public Distribution System scheme, and other benefits, such as domicile certificates. Senior Advocate Rauf Rahim , for petitioners, urged a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana to pass an order that there should not be such a "ripple effect" following exclusion from electoral rolls due to SIR. The bench however did not record pass any such order. CJI Surya Kant said that the Court was now only focusing on issues relating to the pending appeals in the tribunals, and other issues can be raised before the High Court. When Rauf submitted that one word from the Supreme Court can prevent such "ripple effects" of SIR exclusions, Justice Bagchi said that in the Bihar SIR judgment , the Court had clarified the effect of electoral roll exclusion over a person's entitlement under social welfare schemes. "We have already clarified our position. In the Bihar SIR judgment, we had made clear that what is the [...] and the exclusion from the voters list qua rights of an individual in social security schemes", Justice Bagchi said. Notably, in the Bihar SIR judgment, the Court had held that ECI cannot decide citizenship of a person and the conclusions reached by it (after SIR) would be relevant only for electoral purposes. "The Commission is empowered, in the exercise of its constitutional mandate, to undertake a limited enquiry into citizenship for the purpose of satisfying itself as to eligibility for inclusion in the electoral roll. Such an enquiry does not amount to a determination of citizenship in the strict sense, and any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone. The consequence of such a determination is correspondingly limited. It affects the individual's entitlement to be included in the electoral roll, and thereby their right to participate in the electoral process. It does not, however, operate to divest the individual of claims of citizenship, nor does it foreclose a determination of that question by the Competent Authority under the Citizenship Act " the Court had said. The bench observed that persons aggrieved by denial of any social welfare benefits after electoral roll-exclusion have the option to approach the High Court. bihar_raw_news.content: Support our Journalism 9th Anniversary: Free Tote & Mug Subscribe Home India Bihar: Several policemen injured in stone-pelting by protesting students India Bihar: Several policemen injured in stone-pelting by protesting students PTI 25 August, 2026 03:45 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Aug 25 (PTI) Several policemen were injured in stone-pelting by students during a protest march towards the Bihar chief minister’s residence here on Tuesday, prompting the law enforcers to use batons to disperse the agitators, officials said. A large number of BPSC (Bihar Public Service Commission) job aspirants, along with other students, began their pre-announced march from Patna’s Gandhi Maidan and reached the Dak Bungalow crossing, where police detained several individuals. As the police tried to stop the agitators at Dak Bungalow crossing using barricades, the students, who wanted to gherao the CM’s residence, broke through the obstacles, prompting the law enforcers to use water cannons to disperse them, but instead of budging, they broke into a ‘rain dance’, they added. Show Full Article Amid the protests, some students pelted the policemen with stones, injuring several law enforcers, leading to a baton charge to disperse the crowd. A group of farmers protesting against the government’s new township policy also joined the protesting students, displaying posters seeking protection of their land from acquisition. Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township is an 81,730-acre planned urban expansion project aimed at developing Patna as a modern economic hub. Heavy police deployment has been ensured at all major intersections in the city. Additional forces, including CRPF and RAF personnel, were deployed at Dak Bungalow crossing. The students have been protesting at Patna’s Gardanibagh area for weeks, with their main demands including a single-tier examination in BPSC-TRE 4, transparency in the recruitment process, recruitment exams by the Bihar Staff Selection Commission (BSSC) and fair opportunities for Hindi-medium candidates. Citing irregularities in the 70th BPSC exams, the protesting students demanded that the exam be cancelled. PTI PKD SUK ACD This report is auto-generated from PTI news service. bihar_raw_news.title: Prashant Kishor's 10000 Jobs Promise: Will Bihar's Youth Get Work? | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 25, 2026 Bihar’s jobs politics: From promises to reality Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Gyan Bhadra Prashant Kishor has taken the oath as MLA from Bankipur, and the first real scorecard for his politics will likely be written in employment numbers, not vote counts. Jobs and self-employment, more than any other portfolio, will decide whether his new role is seen as substance or spectacle. He has pledged to help 10,000 young people from his constituency find work. Barely has the promise settled when Purnea MP Pappu Yadav, who has long positioned himself as a benefactor of Bihar’s job seekers, raised the stakes further — announcing that 30-40 companies will visit Purnea, reportedly with Rahul Gandhi in attendance, to offer jobs to roughly the same number of youths. Two politicians, two nearly identical figures, one obvious question: whose number is bigger matters far less than how many of these jobs actually show up on the ground. Kishor’s plan leans on personal capital rather than public office. He has said he intends to draw on his corporate contacts to link unemployed youth with hiring companies, and has reportedly travelled outside Bihar recently to meet business associates toward that end. Manoj Bharti, Jan Suraaj’s state president, has been blunt about what this means in practice: these will be private-sector jobs, not government ones, and most will be located outside Bihar altogether, since — in his own assessment — the state lacks companies capable of absorbing that scale of hiring. That distinction between government and private employment is not incidental; it is central to Kishor’s own argument. During the 2025 Bihar assembly campaign, he pointed out that only about 23 lakh people have entered government service across all 75 years of Bihar’s history — from peon to chief secretary — a mere 1.97 percent of the state’s population. Even raising reservation to 100 percent on the ten lakh government jobs politicians love to cite, he noted, would still leave 98 percent of Biharis outside the government payroll. That reality is what pushed him toward a private-sector, network-driven route instead — and it’s a route with a structural limit built in: an MLA has no authority to hand out private jobs. At best, Kishor can be a matchmaker between companies and candidates, which makes his promise unusually easy to measure and unusually easy to expose if it falls short. The metrics that will actually matter go well beyond how many young people submit applications. What counts is how many get interviews, how many receive offer letters, and — critically — how many are still employed six months or a year later. A job that evaporates after a few weeks, or one that pays too little to change a family’s fortunes, cannot honestly be called employment generation. Pappu Yadav’s Purnea initiative invites the same scrutiny. Company visits and Rahul Gandhi’s high-profile presence generate headlines, but neither tells us how many actual vacancies exist or how many candidates will walk out with a job. Bihar

bihar_raw_news.title: TN announces Rs 25 crore under CM's urban development mission for infrastructure projects
bihar_raw_news.content: Tamil Development Minister A Rajmohan. (File photo | Express) Tamil Nadu TN announces Rs 25 crore under CM’s urban development mission for infrastructure projects Integrated drinking water schemes were announced for 286 roadside settlements in Kanyakumari district and for Srivilliputhur municipality in Virudhunagar district and two municipalities and seven town panchayats in Tenkasi. Express News Service Updated: 25th Aug, 2026 at 8:00 AM CHENNAI: The state government on Monday announced a series of infrastructure and civic projects under the Municipal Administration and Water Supply department, covering water supply, solid waste management, underground sewerage system network, and others, across all local bodies. Speaking in the Assembly, Minister A Rajmohan said detailed project reports would be prepared under the Chief Minister’s Integrated Urban Development Mission at an estimated Rs 25 crore across all corporations, municipalities, and town panchayats, focusing on drinking water, sewerage, solid waste management, roads, urban greening and restoration of water bodies. Among the key announcements, 22 sewage treatment plants run by the Metro Water will be upgraded to produce compressed biogas. Integrated drinking water schemes were announced for 286 roadside settlements in Kanyakumari district and for Srivilliputhur municipality in Virudhunagar district and two municipalities and seven town panchayats in Tenkasi. In Tambaram Corporation, sewerage reconstruction in Pallavaram and Chrompet zones and a new UGD project will be established in Thiruneermalai at a total cost of Rs 254 crore. Feasibility studies for city-wide underground sewerage in Coimbatore, Sivakasi and Tiruchendur will be conducted. During the debate, DMK MLA KN Nehru urged the state government to increase the number of wards in urban local bodies ahead of the upcoming local body elections. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Approves Six-Lane Greenfield Corridor from Buxar to Bhagalpur - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Approves Six-Lane Greenfield Corridor from Buxar to Bhagalpur 24 Aug 2026 1 min read Why in News? The Bihar Cabinet , chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary , approved a 336-km six-lane greenfield corridor connecting Buxar with Bhagalpur . Key Points Six-Lane Corridor: A 336-km six-lane greenfield road corridor will connect Buxar with Bhagalpur . The corridor will pass through Bhojpur, Arwal, Jehanabad, Nalanda, Munger, Sheikhpura, Banka, Gaya, Nawada, Jamui and Lakhisarai before reaching Bhagalpur. Implementation: The project will be implemented through the Bihar State Road Development Corporation Limited (BSRDCL) . The Cabinet approved the appointment of consultants and a transaction adviser for preparation of the Detailed Project Report (DPR). AI-Based Infrastructure: Bihar’s Information Technology Department has signed an MoU with Japanese company Tayo to develop an AI-based infrastructure platform . The platform will help in identifying and prioritising infrastructure projects, monitoring their progress and supporting implementation. Economic Development: The corridor is expected to promote agriculture, trade and other economic activities across the districts along its route. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called upon young diplomats to build strong grassroots-level engagement in their countries of posting and deepen India’s connection with local communities. Interacting with the Officer Trainees of the 2025 Batch of the Indian Foreign Service (IFS) at Seva Teerth, Mr Modi encouraged the Officer Trainees to expand their networks beyond traditional diplomatic circles and deepen engagement with people. Akashvani correspondent reports that PM Modi encouraged the officer trainees to combine India’s civilisational strengths with technology, innovation and effective communication to further strengthen India’s global engagement. The Prime Minister also called upon the Officer Trainees to serve as catalytic agents for the country’s economic engagement with the world. He also emphasised the importance of strengthening the digital presence of Indian Missions. Mr Modi urged the Officer Trainees to work towards making India a more attractive global tourism destination by showcasing its civilisational, cultural and geographical strengths. He suggested leveraging the “Bharat ko Janiye” (Know India) Quiz to generate greater interest in India among young people across the world and encouraged the use of AI and gaming to make such initiatives more engaging. The Officer Trainees shared their experiences from training and Bharat Darshan. The group comprised 50 IFS Officer Trainees who came from different States and Union Territories across the country.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 635 HM Amit Shah directs agencies to intensify measures against infiltration, use AI to counter natio...
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has directed all agencies to take strict measures against infiltration. Inaugurating the 9th National Security Strategies Conference-2026 in New Delhi, Mr. Shah directed that an AI-based analysis of information available on Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) platforms should be done to create SOPs to counter various national security challenges. To effectively tackle terrorism and radicalisation, Mr. Shah emphasised training for the implementation of the Home Ministry’s PRAHAAR scheme, expediting trials by bringing back fugitives and utilising trial in absentia provisions, and undertaking a comprehensive and integrated approach while investigating UAPA cases. On the first day of the Conference, discussions focused on critical aspects of national security, including response to counter-terrorism challenges, fusion, analysis, and operationalisation of intelligence through the Multi-Agency Centre (MAC), a vision document on narcotics control, detection and deportation of illegal migrants, a policy framework to combat cybercrime, and proxy warfare by Pakistan. Prior to the inauguration, Mr Shah paid homage at the Martyrs’ Column by laying a wreath in remembrance of the brave personnel of the Intelligence Bureau who made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty to safeguard national security and integrity. The two-day conference is being held in a hybrid format and is being attended by over 850 participants from across the country. Ministers of State for Home Affairs, Union Home Secretary, Deputy National Security Advisors, Heads of Central Armed Police Forces, and Central Police Organisations attended the conference in Delhi. DGsP of States and UTs, young police officers working at the cutting-edge level, and domain experts from specialised fields joined the conference through virtual mode. On the second day today, the Conference will focus on the threat landscape from sub-aerial systems and formulating countermeasures, securing the blue economy, information warfare and its implications on national security, and the need for a biosecurity framework. Pursuant to the directions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the conference is being held every year in a hybrid format since 2021, with the objective of finding solutions to major national security challenges using the extensive experience of cutting-edge officers working at the grassroots level in collaboration with domain experts.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 100 NSA Ajit Doval to hold Special Representatives’ Talks with Chinese Foreign Minister on India-Chin...
national_raw_news.content: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval will hold the 25th round of Special Representatives’ Talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on the India-China Boundary issue in Beijing today. The two leaders will have an in-depth discussion on the boundary question as well as other bilateral, regional and international issues. Mr Doval will also call on China’s Vice President Han Zheng during his visit. The National Security Advisor arrived in Beijing yesterday on a two-day visit to China. Ahead of the Doval-Wang talks, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar reiterated that “peace and tranquillity” along the border areas are a prerequisite for good relations with China. Both Mr Doval and Mr Wang are the designated Special Representatives for the boundary talks mechanism, which was established in 2003 to comprehensively address the dispute over the India-China border. The China-India Special Representatives’ Talks are the main channel for negotiations between the two countries on the boundary issue. It is also an important platform for communication between the two sides on issues of mutual interest. In August last year, China and India successfully held the 24th round of talks, during which the two sides had candid and in-depth exchanges of views on the boundary question and reached a number of common understandings.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 122 UPI completes 10 years of Digital Payments Revolution; Clocks nearly 13,000-fold rise in transact...
national_raw_news.content: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has completed ten years of transforming digital payments and has emerged as the backbone of India’s digital payments ecosystem. The UPI, which was launched on 25th August 2016, has surged almost 13 thousand fold in transaction volume. Akashvani correspondent reports that the Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume expanded from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24 thousand 162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from seven thousand crore to nearly 314 lakh crore during the same time period. The Ministry said that UPI has also emerged as a global platform for cross-border digital payments and is currently operational in 11 countries. These are the United Arab Emirates, France, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Singapore, Mauritius, Qatar, Cambodia, Greece and the Maldives. UPI has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an interoperable, real-time payments platform. Today, it is the preferred mode of payment for millions of users, transforming the way India transacts. By bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have received global recognition. It said, the International Monetary Fund has acknowledged it as the world’s largest real‑time payment system. As of 2025, UPI accounts for nearly 49 per cent of the world’s real-time payment transaction volume.

national_raw_news.title: Puducherry Govt introduces Puducherry Business Reforms Bill, 2026 4 mins ago 2
national_raw_news.content: The Government of Puducherry today introduced the Puducherry Business Reforms Bill, 2026, aimed at making the Union Territory a simpler, faster and more investment-friendly destination for businesses and entrepreneurs. The Bill seeks to shift business regulation from permission-based control to rule-based governance, with emphasis on transparency, predictability and time-bound decision-making. A major focus of the Bill is on MSMEs and entrepreneurship. It proposes to extend the exemption from approvals for MSMEs to five years, with a further one-year extension, and introduce auto-generation of Acknowledgement Certificates if they are not issued within the prescribed time. Invest Puducherry will also be strengthened as a single point of contact for investors. The Bill proposes greater flexibility in land use and development regulations, rationalisation of building and zoning requirements, and removal of duplicative and obsolete compliances. An auto-appeal mechanism is also proposed to enable applicants to appeal against rejection without a separate procedural process. The Government said the reforms will reduce regulatory burden while protecting safeguards relating to public safety, fire and structural safety, environment, pollution control, labour safety, public health and land rights. The Bill seeks to advance the “Minimum Government, Maximum Facilitation” approach and strengthen Puducherry as a destination for investment, enterprise, innovation and employment.

national_raw_news.title: Justice Sunil Balkrishna Shukre becomes new Chairman of Maharashtra Lokayukta Institution 6 mins ago 4
national_raw_news.content: Justice Sunil Balkrishna Shukre, former Judge of the Bombay High Court, was sworn in as the new Chairman of the Maharashtra Lokayukta Institution today. Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma administered the oath of office to Justice Shukre at a brief oath-taking ceremony held at Lok Bhavan, Mumbai. The oath was given as per Section VI of the newly passed Maharashtra Lokayukta Act, 2023. The appointment of Justice Shukre has been made for a period of 5 years or till he attains the age of 70, whichever is earlier. Justice Sunil Shukre graduated from Pune University in 1980, and did his LL.B. in 1983 from Dr. Punjabrao Deshmukh Law College, Amravati, affiliated to the then Nagpur University. He stood second in the Order of Merit at the LL.B. examination and is the recipient of the Late Kale Memorial Prize for having secured the highest marks in Hindu law at the the LL.B. examination. He commenced his legal practice at Amravati. He did LL.M. in Constitutional Law from the then Nagpur University. He has a keen interest in sports and has represented M.J. College, Jalgaon in Inter-collegiate tournaments in Lawn Tennis and Badminton. He joined the Judiciary as a Direct District Judge from Bar in the year 2000 and since then has worked as Principal District Judge, Kolhapur, Registrar (Administration), Nagpur Bench of Bombay High Court, Joint Director, Maharashtra Judicial Academy, Uttan, Thane, Principal District Judge, Nagpur and took charge as Registrar General, High Court Bombay on 17th March, 2011. Elevated as Judge of the Bombay High Court on 13th May, 2013. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Adv. Rahul Narwekar, MLA Bhaskar Jadhav, outgoing Lokayukta Justice (retd) Vidyasagar Kanade, Chief Secretary Rajesh Aggaral, Members of the Lokayukta Institution, Justice Sandeep Shinde, Lokayukta of Goa, State Chief Information Commissioner Rahul Pande and senior government officers were present.
